turn.speech: Supabase offers daily backups on paid plans, PITR as a paid add-on with about a two minute worst-case recovery point, and manual dumps for all plans. A scenario: a table was dropped at 14:03 and noticed at 14:20. Which recovery point would you pick, and what happens to data written in between?
turn.text:
Supabase has three backup mechanisms on hosted projects. The sources were fetched on 2026-10-21. Verify prices live before you commit to anything.

## 1. Daily backups (Pro, Team, Enterprise)

- Pro, Team and Enterprise projects are backed up automatically every day [1]. You can find them under **Database > Backups** in the Dashboard [1].
- Retention is 7 days on Pro, 14 days on Team and up to 30 days on Enterprise [1].
- The docs list automatic daily backups only for Pro, Team and Enterprise projects [1]. For Free projects they recommend regular exports with `supabase db dump` and off-site copies [1].

## 2. Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR, paid add-on)

- **Availability:** Pro, Team and Enterprise projects can enable PITR as an add-on, and the project must also have at least a Small compute add-on [2].
- **Mechanism:** It combines a daily physical snapshot with continuously archived WAL files, handled by WAL-G [2].
- **RPO:** WAL is backed up every two minutes by default, or sooner if the files exceed a size threshold [2]. When the database is idle, no WAL is archived [2]. The worst-case recovery point objective (RPO) is two minutes [2].
- **Interaction with daily backups:** Enabling PITR stops the separate daily backups, because PITR is finer-grained [2].
- **Restore:** You pick a time within the earliest and latest recovery points [3]. Supabase restores the latest physical backup, then replays WAL up to your target time [3]. The project is inaccessible during the restore, and downtime grows with database size [3].
- **Cost:** The pricing page lists PITR at $100 per month per 7 days of retention [4]. The add-on is not covered by the Spend Cap [5].
- **Downloads:** If you later disable PITR, new backups are physical only and can't be downloaded directly [6]. For a downloadable copy you need a manual logical backup with the CLI or `pg_dump` [6].

## 3. Manual logical backups (all plans)

- You can run `supabase db dump` or `pg_dump` yourself [1][6]. For Free projects this is the approach the docs recommend [1].
- A logical dump captures the database at the moment you run it. It has no point-in-time granularity. This is my inference from how a dump works, not a statement from the docs.

## Comparison

| Option | Plans | Granularity | Extra cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Daily backups | Pro / Team / Enterprise [1] | Once per day, kept 7 / 14 / up to 30 days [1] | Included in the plan [1] |
| PITR | Pro / Team / Enterprise, Small compute or larger [2] | Worst-case RPO of about 2 minutes [2] | $100/month per 7 days of retention [4] |
| Manual dump | All | Moment of the dump (inference) | None, but you run it and store it |

## Caveats

- Deleting a project permanently removes all associated data, including its backups stored in S3 [1]. A Supabase backup does not replace an off-site copy.
- A backup you have never restored is unproven, so test a restore on a non-production project.

Question: a Pro project has PITR enabled with 7-day retention. A developer runs `DROP TABLE orders` at 14:03, and you notice at 14:20. Which recovery point would you pick, and what happens to the data written between 14:03 and 14:20?
